We need to determine the crime(s) for the given facts.

Facts: Li, a financial audit chief, was responsible for financial checks of grain stations. He discovered that station chief Huang had embezzled public funds (240+ million) for personal use. Li, during 2013-2014 checks, found the borrowing but did not report in meeting, only privately reminded Huang. Li's work is serious dereliction of duty. The prosecution wants to hold Li criminally responsible.

What crime? Likely "滥用职权" (abuse of power) or "徇私舞弊不移交刑事案件" (but that is for officials not handing over criminal cases). Here Li failed to report the crime, which is a dereliction of duty. In Chinese criminal law, there is a crime "滥用职权罪" (abuse of power) for officials who abuse authority to cause loss. But here he didn't abuse authority to cause loss, he just failed to report. There is also "徇私舞弊不移交刑事案件" (private collusion, not handing over criminal case). That is for law enforcement officials who fail to hand over criminal cases. But Li is a financial auditor, not law enforcement. There is also "滥用职权" (abuse of power) which may apply for officials who fail to perform duties leading to loss. However the list includes "滥用职权". Also "失职" is not in list. The list includes "滥用职权". So likely the charge is "滥用职权". Also maybe "徇私舞弊不移交刑事案件" but that is specific to not handing over criminal cases. The fact says he didn't report to leadership, just privately reminded. That could be considered "徇私舞弊不移交刑事案件". But the phrase "不移交刑事案件" means not handing over a criminal case to the authorities. He didn't report to the authorities. He is a public official, his duty is to report. So that fits.

Which label is more appropriate? In previous examples, "徇私舞弊不移交刑事案件" used for health supervision officials who didn't hand over illegal medical cases. Here it's a financial auditor not reporting embezzlement. Could be similar.

The list includes "滥用职权". That is more generic for abusing authority. He didn't abuse authority, he just omitted reporting. The crime of "徇私舞弊不移交刑事案件" is about failing to hand over criminal cases. That matches.

Thus answer: [罪名]徇私舞弊不移交刑事案件<eoa>

Check list: "徇私舞弊不移交刑事案件" exactly present. Yes.

Thus final answer.
